description: Owner-approved numeric claims outside the treatment architecture (Stage 9.48). A figure in a member-facing file is explained by an entry here only when the entry's market, owning resource, context patterns and label requirement all match the sentence it appears in. Treatment figures are NOT here: admin-import/config/treatment-sources.json owns them, and the scanner defers to it. Figures inside an owner-approved safety block are covered by that block's own recorded sources in safety-blocks.json. Stage 9.52 adds the "ratio" claim type for unitless dilution ratios ("four parts vinegar to one part water", "half and half"): a ratio of volumes is still a volume claim, so it is detected as a capacity candidate and blocks under the capacity activation rather than needing a new blocking category. Ratio detection requires a mixing or diluting context and refuses to read a scoring instrument — a 1-5 room score, a "10-20 = Critical" band, "out of 5" — as chemistry.
status: OWNER-APPROVED 2026-09-23 (Stage 9.50) - BLOCKING for the approved first activation. Percentage and currency are detected and reported but do not block. Extended 2026-09-23 (Stage 9.52) with the ratio claim type and the twelve Air-block figures.
seedingRule: Seeded only from Bucket A: figures whose source is recorded in approved stage work. Nothing is seeded from memory, nothing from Bucket C, and no citation is invented.

value.text: test monthly; vacuum or dust every six months; check the expiry date and replace a 9V battery every year; replace the alarm every ten years

claims.allowedWording: Fire and Emergency New Zealand's maintenance routine: once a month press the test button; every six months vacuum or dust; every year check the expiry date and replace a 9V battery; every ten years replace the alarm.
match: \bOnce a month,? press the test button\b
\bEvery ten years,? replace your smoke alarms\b
\bFire and Emergency New Zealand\b[\s\S]{0,400}\b(?:once a month|every six months|every ten years)\b
limitations: New Zealand only. The Australian intervals are published by state fire services, differ in detail (a five-second test hold, 12-monthly batteries) and must not be merged with these.
The ten-year figure is a REPLACEMENT interval, not an age pass/fail test: the legacy 'under 10 years old' wording is not what FENZ publishes and must not be reinstated.
Hard-wired alarms follow the installer's schedule; this routine does not override a manufacturer's instructions.

The routine is written one instruction per sentence and must be introduced by Fire and Emergency New Zealand in the same block; the patterns match FENZ's own wording, not any monthly or six-monthly interval.

claims.allowedWording: if the alarm takes a 9V battery, replace the battery every year (Fire and Emergency New Zealand)

It is a placement distance from a bedroom door. It approves 'three metres' of nothing else — not a clearance, not a setback, not a generator distance.

value.text: half and half — equal parts white vinegar and water, on painted surfaces

claims.allowedWording: Tenancy Services says white vinegar is a cheap and effective way to clean mould, and that on painted surfaces you should dilute the vinegar with water, half and half, to avoid damaging the paint.
match: \bdilute the vinegar with water, half and half\b
limitations: New Zealand's dilution. New South Wales publishes a different one (four parts vinegar to one part water) and the two must never cross.
It is a dilution to protect PAINT, in a method whose purpose is removing mould. It carries no efficacy claim: no 'kills mould' wording may be attached to it.
It approves no bleach ratio. Tenancy Services' bleach alternative (one part bleach to three parts water) is WITHHELD pending an owner ruling and has no entry here.
